End Barrens: The End barrens biome is a biome used to generate the outer End islands.
End Highlands: The End highlands is a biome used to generate the outer End islands.
End Midlands: The End midlands is a biome used to generate outer End islands.
Small End Islands: The small End islands biome is a biome used to generate outer End islands.
Soul Sand Valley: A soul sand valley is a dry biome located in the Nether. It is formed of large caverns with Nether fossils and different blocks, mainly including soul sand and soul soil.
The End (biome): The End is a biome used to generate the End dimension. There are five biomes in the End, but they are considered separate biomes only in Java Edition. Outer End islands are generated by a different mechanism in Bedrock Edition.
Warped Forest: The warped forest is an uncommon forested biome found in the Nether. Endermen are common in this biome, and hostile mobs do not spawn naturally. It is one of two Nether biomes where players are able to acquire wood without returning to the Overworld. The warped forest is the only place where huge warped fungus trees grow naturally.
Grove: A grove is a snowy forest biome that often generates on the sides of mountains. Similar to the snowy taiga, it is filled with spruce trees but the ground is covered with snow blocks and occasional powder snow patches.
Ice Spikes: The ice spikes or ice plains spikes is a variant of the snowy plains, featuring ice spikes made of packed ice and other special features.
Jagged Peaks: The jagged peaks are one of the three tall mountain peak biomes. These tall and jagged mountains are completely made out of stone covered by a layer of snow blocks.
Jungle: A jungle is a lush biome with dense vegetation of jungle trees, oak trees, bamboo, and various smaller plants. Jungles generate in humid and warm areas, often next to forests, and their sparse and bamboo variants.
Lukewarm Ocean: The lukewarm ocean is a lukewarm variant of oceans.
Lush Caves: The lush caves is a temperate cave biome with unique fauna and flora found underground below humid biomes, indicated above ground by azalea trees. Exclusive mobs, such as the axolotl, glow squid, and tropical fish can spawn here.
Mangrove Swamp: The mangrove swamp is a wetland biome populated with mud and mangroves where slimes, frogs, and bogged can spawn.
Meadow: The meadow is an elevated grassy mountain slope biome filled with patches of flowers, turquoise-green grass and tall grass, where sheep, donkeys and rabbits spawn.
Mountains: Mountains are terrain forms with elevated and jagged terrain, containing unique biomes and terrain characteristics.
Mushroom Fields: Mushroom fields or mushroom islands are rare biomes which always generate as islands surrounded by deep oceans. They are the only place in the game where mycelium and mooshrooms are found, and have the special property that no hostile mobs normally spawn in them.
Ocean: The ocean is an aquatic biome consisting of water. They are deep bodies of water with the surface at an altitude of Y=63 by default, which is counted as the “sea level” of the world.
Ocean biomes: This page is an overview of all ocean biomes.
Old Growth Birch Forest: An old growth birch forest or birch forest mutated is a variant of the birch forest, notable for its trees, which are taller than those found in the normal birch forest.
Old Growth Pine Taiga: Old growth pine taigas or mega taigas are forested biomes covered with both large 2×2 and normal-sized spruce trees, with the tall trees being mostly arrow shaped with few leaves at the top. Uniquely to this biome, Zombie villagers have the highest spawn rate amongst all biomes‌[Java Edition  only].
Old Growth Spruce Taiga: The old growth spruce taiga or redwood taiga mutated is a forested biome covered with tall spruce trees.
Pale Garden: A pale garden is a rare pale variant of the dark forest biome. It features pale oaks, pale moss blocks, and pale moss carpets. Creaking hearts that spawn creakings at night can often be found here.
Plains: The plains is a common grassland biome in the Overworld that usually generates in flat terrain.
River: A river is a common aquatic biome that cuts through most land biomes. Rivers can serve as borders between various other biomes, and usually lead to oceans, although they are also able to form loops.
Savanna: The savanna is an arid grassland biome, featuring scattered acacia and oak trees. It is populated by warm animal variants, llamas, and armadillos, and villages made of acacia wood are commonly found here.
Savanna Plateau: A savanna plateau is a variant of the savanna biome that replaces it at higher elevations. The biome features spotted wolves  unlike the regular savanna, and lacks villages and pillager outposts.
Badlands: The badlands or mesa are arid-land mountainous biomes, featuring red sand and mounds of terracotta bands, coming in various colors.
Bamboo Jungle: A bamboo jungle is a variant of the jungle with dense bamboo growth and large jungle trees. Pandas are abundant in this biome.
Beach: Beaches are common coastal biomes that serve as transition biomes from the mainland to an ocean. Beaches are covered entirely with sand and are the main source of turtles and buried treasures.
Birch Forest: A birch forest is a lush biome filled with birch trees and wildflowers that usually generates near other woodland biomes.
Cherry Grove: A cherry grove is a mountain slope and plateau biome similar to meadows, filled with cherry trees.
Cold Ocean: The cold ocean is a cold variant of the ocean biome. It generates near cold biomes and has a deep variant.
Dark Forest: A dark forest or roofed forest is a forested biome with dense leaf canopies that block sunlight, allowing hostile mobs to spawn and hide from the sun during daytime. Dark Forests are one of the two biomes that Woodland Mansions can generate in.
Deep Cold Ocean: The deep cold ocean is a deep variant of cold oceans.
Deep Dark: The deep dark is a cave biome that generates deep underground in the Overworld under mountainous areas.
Deep Frozen Ocean: The deep frozen ocean is a deep variant of frozen oceans. Unlike the regular frozen ocean, the water surface is not covered with ice, though icebergs still generate in the water.
Deep Lukewarm Ocean: The deep lukewarm ocean is a deep variant of lukewarm oceans.
Deep Ocean: A deep ocean is a deeper variant of oceans.
Desert: A desert is an expansive arid biome mainly consisting of sand.
Dripstone Caves: The dripstone caves is a cave biome found in inland areas, filled with clusters and pillars of pointed dripstone and dripstone blocks.
Eroded Badlands: The eroded badlands or mesa bryce is a variant of the badlands notable for its hoodoos.
Flower Forest: A flower forest is a variant of the forest filled with a much larger variation and frequency of flowers. Rabbits spawn here instead of wolves and bee nests generate much more often.
Forest: The forest is a lush biome densely wooded with oak and birch trees. Wolves spawn here. The forest is the most common surface biome in Minecraft, making up about 12% of the Overworld's area.
Frozen Ocean: The frozen ocean is a cold variant of oceans covered by icebergs. The water's surface is partially covered with ice, where snowfall may occur and polar bears can spawn.
Frozen Peaks: Frozen peaks are snowy mountain peak biomes made out of ice and packed ice covered by snow blocks.
Frozen River: A frozen river is an ice topped variant of the river that replaces it in cold regions.
Basalt Deltas: The basalt deltas are a volcanic biome found in the Nether.
Crimson Forest: The crimson forest is a forested biome in the Nether. It is one of two Nether biomes where players are able to acquire wood without returning to the Overworld. This forest is the only place where huge crimson fungus trees grow naturally.
Nether Wastes: The Nether wastes or hell‌[Bedrock Edition  only] is the most common biome found in the Nether.
Snowy Beach: A snowy beach or cold beach is a snowy variant of the beach biome that replaces it in snowy regions.
Snowy Plains: The snowy plains or ice plains are snow-covered grassland biomes in the Overworld that usually generate near other snowy biomes.
Snowy Slopes: Snowy slopes are snowy biomes that often generate on the sides of mountains. Unlike the snowy plains, this biome is made out of stone covered with one or more layers of snow blocks and occasional powder snow patches.
Snowy Taiga: A snowy taiga or cold taiga is an icy biome that comprises a snow-covered forest of pine and spruce trees, ferns and large ferns, and sweet berry bushes, usually generating adjacent to or within snowy plains.
Sparse Jungle: The sparse jungle or jungle edge biome is a sparser variant of the jungle, resembling a lush plains biome with small jungle trees.
Stony Peaks: Stony peaks are warmer mountain peak biomes completely made out of stone and calcite strips.
Stony Shore: A stony shore or stone beach is a coastal biome that is almost entirely made of stone and gravel. Stony shores replace beach biomes in some mountainous areas.
Sulfur Caves: The sulfur caves is a cave biome composed of sulfur and cinnabar blocks, where sulfur cubes and cave spiders spawn. Sulfur pools with potent sulfur generate here, in addition to sulfur spikes.
Sunflower Plains: Sunflower plains are flat grasslands biomes that generate with sunflowers. They are the only places where sunflowers naturally generate.
Swamp: A swamp or swampland is a wetland biome where slimes, frogs, and bogged can spawn.
Taiga: The taiga is a humid and cold biome comprising a grassland forested with small and large ferns, pale aquamarine-green grass, spruce and pine trees. Foxes commonly spawn here.
Warm Ocean: The warm ocean is a warm variant of oceans filled with coral reefs on a sand-covered floor. Tropical fish and pufferfish spawn here, and sea pickles can generate on the ocean floor.
Windswept Forest: The windswept forest or extreme hills plus trees is a more humid variant of the windswept hills biome filled with spruce and oak trees.
Windswept Gravelly Hills: The windswept gravelly hills or extreme hills mutated is a slightly altered and more desolate variant of the windswept hills covered with gravel. It is a relatively rare biome in the Overworld.
Windswept Hills: Windswept hills or extreme hills are cold mountainous biomes with shattered terrain covered by grass blocks and stone. Windswept hills generate in areas with high erosion close to swamps, often bordering their wooded and gravelly variants.
Windswept Savanna: The windswept savanna or savanna mutated is a shattered and mountainous variant of savanna that generates in areas with high erosion close to swamps and other windswept biomes. The terrain consists of huge cliffs and floating islands covered with coarse dirt, stone, and the regular savanna vegetation.
Wooded Badlands: The wooded badlands or mesa plateau stone is a more humid variant of the badlands covered by oak trees, grass blocks, and coarse dirt.
